# FED Build Manual — Manual UI Build & Delivery

**Owner:** Marcel Angelo Navarro · **Started:** August 2026

This is the guide to building the UI manually — not via a Figma-to-React generator. F2R outputs are an
input we leverage where they exist; they are not the delivery mechanism. You are writing the component.

Read §3 (Design Foundations) before your first component. It contains traps that will cost you time
each if you meet them by surprise.

---

## 1. The Operating Principles

Four things were agreed that change how you build. They apply to every story.

### Static-first

Where an integration isn't available yet, **build against static data and move on.** Do not block, and
do not stub out a fake integration layer.

- Props in, markup out. The component takes the data it renders as props.
- Static/mock data lives in the **story**, not in the component.
- No data-fetching hooks inside `overrides/app/components/` — that's the container/presentational rule
  in `.claude/rules/components.md`, and it's what makes the later wiring a one-file change instead of
  a rewrite.

When Contentful (or SFCC, or Omneo) comes online, the component doesn't change — the page or container
that feeds it does. If you find yourself writing "temporary" fetch logic inside a component, stop:
that's the thing static-first exists to prevent.

### Leverage what exists before building

In priority order — this is the ladder, and you should be able to say which rung you landed on:

```
Salesforce / PWA Kit base capability
        ↓  nothing fits
Existing shared component in overrides/
        ↓  nothing fits
Existing pattern in the codebase
        ↓  nothing fits
New implementation  ← justify this in the PR description
```

F2R outputs count as "existing": the onshore design team's outputs, Jersey's work (currently mostly
primitive/foundation-level), and the design foundations now in the codebase. Use them where they fit
rather than starting clean.

**The default is override, not build.** Not for tidiness — because an override **inherits the wiring for
free.** Override `product-view` and you get `addToCart([{product, variant, quantity}])`, the add-to-cart
modal, bundle handling and `updateCart` already connected. Build a bespoke equivalent and every one of
those has to be re-derived, re-tested and re-reviewed — none of which is visible in the story points, and
all of which lands on you.

There's a second effect worth understanding, because it changes where your work shows up. PWA Kit's
resolver rewires imports transparently, so **overriding a component that SFCC's own base components
already import means the entire base template inherits your version** — zero call sites touched. A
bespoke component in a new folder only reaches the pages someone remembers to wire it into. Same result
on the page you're building; very different coverage across the site.

⚠️ **One documented exception: `shared/ui/`.** That directory is consumed through a barrel
(`shared/ui/index.jsx`), and the barrel's own re-exports are **relative** (`export {Button} from
'./Button'`). The `ccExtensibility` resolver only rewrites `@salesforce/retail-react-app/...`
specifiers, so a relative import inside `node_modules` is never redirected. **208 base files import
that barrel; none import `shared/ui/Button` directly — so overriding `shared/ui/<Name>/` intercepts
nothing.** It is a place to put raw Zimmermann primitives for *our own* code to import explicitly, not
an interception point. See "Two component families" below.

If you do land on "build custom", expect to justify it in the PR — that's not a formality, it's the one
question review will always ask.

### Figma stays open the whole time

Figma is not a one-time handoff you read and close. Keep it open and use it to actively find problems:

- Validate the build against the design as you go, not at the end.
- Spot **missing tokens** — a value in Figma with no counterpart in `theme/foundation/`.
- Spot **missing design definitions** — a state (hover, disabled, error, empty) with no design.
- Catch discrepancies between design and implementation.

When you find a gap, **raise it** — §7 covers where it goes. Silently inventing a value is the failure
mode; a hardcoded hex that "looked right" is how a design system dies.

**Check the Figma link on the card actually points at your story's frame.** Because we work through the
Figma MCP, that link isn't a reference — it's effectively the spec, and whatever it points at is what
gets built.

A wrong or stale link doesn't announce itself. It produces a component built to the wrong design, AC
signed off against a different frame, and QA testing a third source — none of which surfaces until page
assembly. If the link looks wrong, **ask the BA (Jas) to fix the card**, don't just work it out in a DM.
A verbal fix repairs one person's understanding and leaves the card — which the BA and QA both read —
still wrong.

### Ask in the group chat

Work it out together rather than solo. If you've been stuck more than ~30 minutes, or you're about to
make a decision that affects more than your own component, post it. These threads are how the team
learns as a group — a question you think is basic is usually three people's question.

Claude is part of the workflow where it fits. Treat its output the way you'd treat a colleague's
first draft: useful, and checked before it ships.

### The bar you're building to

Worth knowing, because it explains why review here is stricter than you may be used to:
**the SOW allows no more than 10 defects across the build, and no Sev3.**

Zimmermann is a luxury brand and is exceptionally particular about UI. That combination removes the usual
"ship it, fix it in QA" option — a visual defect that would be a shrug elsewhere consumes part of a very
small budget. Practically, for you:

- Expect UI PRs to be reviewed against the preview environment **and** Figma, not just the diff.
- Self-review the same way before you open it (§8). It's faster than a review round-trip.
- Where design is missing or contradictory, **flag it** rather than picking something plausible. An
  invented value becomes a defect *and* a design-system divergence — two problems instead of none.

---

## 2. Before you write any code

Five minutes here saves a day later.

### Run the session start

```bash
/session-start
```

Reads the tracking docs, checks your branch, states where the project is. Do it once per session.

### Confirm your branch

```bash
git branch --show-current
```

`feature/*` or `fix/*`, branched from `develop`. **If it says `develop` or `main`, stop.** No exceptions.

### Check what already exists

| Question | Where to look |
|---|---|
| Does a Base / Override / Custom component already cover this? | `.claude/registry/components.md` |
| Same for hooks, utils, pages, routes | `.claude/registry/{hooks,utils,pages,routes}.md` |
| What's in the base package? | `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/` |
| Which tier am I about to touch? | Registry `Tier` column, or `/audit-tier <path>` |
| Is another squad the owner? | Registry `Squad` column · `.claude/rules/squad{A,B}.md` |

The registry's **`Origin`** column is the one that matters most:

- **`Custom`** — a Zimmermann component already in `overrides/`. Extend it.
- **`Override`** — a base component already scaffolded into `overrides/`. Edit it directly.
- **`Base`** — it exists upstream but is **not** in `overrides/` yet. **This has a cost.** See below.

### Three component families — and they do different jobs

`overrides/app/components/` holds three kinds of thing. Knowing which you're writing decides the path, the
naming, and whether it affects anything but your own page.

| | `components/<kebab-name>/` | `components/ui-kits/{atoms,molecules}/<camelName>/` | `components/shared/ui/<PascalName>/` |
|---|---|---|---|
| **What it is** | An override of an SFCC component | A Zimmermann design-system component | A raw primitive — Link, Text, Image, Button |
| **Naming** | Keep SFCC's kebab-case exactly (`product-tile/`) | **camelCase** (`zimmButton/`) | Mirror upstream's PascalCase (`Button/`) |
| **Layout** | `index.tsx` + story | `index.tsx` + story, one folder per component | `index.tsx` |
| **Intercepts SFCC?** | **Yes** — base files import by full package path | No | **No** — see the barrel exception above |
| **Who consumes it** | Every base page that used it, plus you | Our own pages and components | Explicit importers — chiefly Contentful renderers |
| **Reach for it when** | Changing how an SFCC component looks or behaves | Building a Zimmermann component from the F2R design library | You want a plain branded primitive, no commerce semantics |

The `shared/ui` family exists because **Contentful renderers need primitives, not commerce components.**
Every Contentful component on `develop` already pulls them in — `duplexSection` (`Box`, `Text`),
`collectionHero` (`Box`, `Button`, `Heading`, `Text`), `hotspotPopup` (`Box`, `Image`, `Link`, `Skeleton`,
`Text`), `imageText`, `heroBanner`, `shoppableImage`. Upstream those resolve to bare Chakra
(`shared/ui/Button/index.jsx` is literally `export {Button} from '@chakra-ui/react'`). A CMS rich-text
renderer mapping a `hyperlink` node to a `Link` wants exactly that — predictable and unopinionated — not a
component carrying SFCC's locale-routing and commerce behaviour.

**Status: the intent is agreed, the wiring is not built.** A `shared/ui/Button` exists on
`feature/pdp-token-class-spike`, its only consumer is the `/dev/components` catalogue page, there is no
`overrides/app/components/shared/ui/index.tsx` barrel, and `collectionHero` still imports `Button` from
the SFCC barrel — so it still gets raw Chakra. Don't build against this family until the barrel question
is settled (see the playbook).

### Atoms and molecules — where they go and what they're called

**Decided.** Zimmermann design-system components live under:

```
overrides/app/components/ui-kits/
  atoms/       zimmButton/  zimmIcon/  zimmLogo/  zimmNavItem/  zimmTextInput/
  molecules/   zimmInputAction/
  organisms/   (when the first one lands)
               └── index.tsx  +  index.stories.tsx
```

**Naming is `camelCase`, one folder per component, `index.tsx` inside.** That follows
`conventions.md` — these are Zimmermann-authored, so camelCase; the kebab-case rule applies *only* to files
mirroring a base Salesforce file, and there is no `@salesforce/…/zimm-button` to mirror. It also satisfies
`components.md`'s rule that **the named export matches the folder name** — `zimmButton/` exports
`ZimmButton`. Precedents already in the repo: `pageContainer/`, `pdpProductInfo/`.

Three casings exist and each is correct in its own family — don't generalise from one to another:

| Family | Casing | Why |
|---|---|---|
| SFCC override | `product-tile/` kebab | Must match upstream; their files import that path |
| **ui-kit component** | **`zimmButton/` camelCase** | **Zimmermann-authored — the default rule** |
| `shared/ui` primitive | `Button/` PascalCase | Mirrors upstream's own PascalCase exactly |

**Which tier?** Atom / molecule / organism is decided by **what the component's own template renders**,
not by how big it looks:

- **Atom** — renders no other component. Markup, CSS and tokens only.
- **Molecule** — renders only atoms.
- **Organism** — renders at least one molecule.

Two rules that settle most arguments: **an icon passed as a prop doesn't count** (`icon="close"` keeps a
Button an atom), and **slotted children don't count** — only what your own template renders. A top bar
composing just Button + Logo is a molecule even though it spans the viewport; tier follows composition,
not pixel size.

If you're porting from the F2R design library, the tier is already recorded there as `composes: [...]` —
use it rather than re-deriving. Add a `@see f2r/02-design/library/elements/<name>` line in the JSDoc so
the link back to the contract survives.

### What's actually overridden today

Worth knowing before you estimate anything: **`overrides/app/components/` currently contains seven
directories.** As of `develop` @ `2dfeb4d`:

```
_app-config   button   contentful   foundation   header   icons   pageContainer
```

That's it. `product-tile`, `display-price`, `swatch-group`, `image-gallery`, `link`, `footer`,
`list-menu`, `drawer-menu` and `seo` are all still **`Origin = Base`** — they exist upstream and are
referenced throughout `.claude/rules/` and the protected-file lists, but they have **not** been scaffolded
into `overrides/` yet.

Two consequences:

- **Most stories you pick up will pay copy-first** (below). Assume it until the registry says otherwise.
- **When a rules file points at one of those as an example, the file won't be there.** The convention is
  real; the worked example often isn't yet. Check before you go looking.

### If `Origin = Base`, the copy-first rule applies

Before any functional work, AGENTS.md requires:

1. Copy the base file → mirrored path in `overrides/` (keep the kebab-case filename exactly)
2. Convert to TypeScript (`.ts`/`.tsx`), fix imports
3. `npx tsc --noEmit`
4. Add a temporary `console.log('[overrides] product-tile.tsx')` marker
5. **Stop.** A human confirms the override is rendering instead of the base
6. Then build; remove the markers

It's serialised and human-gated, and **the first story against a given base component pays it — later
ones don't.** This is the single most common reason a story looks small and isn't. Flag it at refinement,
not on day three of the sprint.

### Sanity-check the scope

```bash
/scope-check
```

Classifies everything you're about to touch by tier and tells you if the change is safe, risky, or
blocked. Worth it any time you're not certain.

---

## 3. Design Foundations — read this before your first component

**Canonical reference: `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md`.** That file is the authority on styling an
override; this section is the orientation for it. If the two ever disagree, the rules file wins — and
this section needs a fix, so raise it.

The design system lives in `overrides/app/theme/`. It has **one** source of truth and derives outward:

```
foundation/  colour.ts · typography.ts · spacing.ts · sizes.ts · motion.ts · gridSystem.ts
        |  imported and derived from — never retyped
foundation/zimmTokens.ts          -> the --zimm-* CSS custom properties
        |  consumed by
theme/components/*.ts (recipes)   ·   globalStyles.ts (.zimm-* classes)
```

`zimmTokens.ts` is **derived**, not a second copy — it imports `colors.grey[900]` rather than retyping
`#191919`. That is why you never edit it directly, and why two values cannot drift apart.
`theme/index.test.tsx` guards the arrangement with 125 tests; a failure there is a real drift signal,
not test noise.

### The styling hierarchy — reach for these in order

This is the load-bearing rule of the whole section.

1. **`textStyle` prop** for anything textual — `textStyle="body2"`, never a raw `fontSize`
2. **Semantic token strings** — `color="text.default"`, `bg="background.02"`,
   `padding={{ base: 'm', md: 'xl' }}`
3. **The component's own `theme/components/<name>.ts`** for anything that varies by variant / size /
   state. For an interactive component with Chakra support (buttons, inputs, links) that file is the
   **single source of truth**
4. **`sx` prop** for a genuine one-off gap in the Chakra prop system
5. **Scoped `.scss`** only when `sx` truly cannot express it (complex pseudo-selectors, keyframes)

**Never** a raw hex / px / rem / em literal in a component file. The one standing exception is
`button.ts`'s provisional constants — trap 2 below.

Registered component recipes today: `Button`, `Header`, `ListMenu` (`theme/components/index.ts`).
Adding a new one is yours to do — one file per Chakra component, registered in that index.

### Setting type — always `textStyle`, never `fontSize`

```tsx
<Text textStyle="body1">…</Text>          // ✅
<Heading textStyle="heading3">…</Heading>  // ✅
<Text fontSize="md">…</Text>               // ❌ never
```

**Why this is a hard rule, not a preference.** Four Zimmermann font-size keys collide with Chakra
defaults, and the base retail-react-app uses those names at ~199 call sites:

| Key | Zimmermann | Chakra |
|---|---|---|
| `md` | 24px | 16px |
| `xs` | 16px | 12px |
| `2xs` | 14px | 10px |
| `3xs` | 12px | 7.2px |

The Zimmermann font scale is **deliberately not registered** as `theme.fontSizes` for exactly this
reason. If you write `fontSize="md"` expecting 24px you get 16px. If you "fix" that by registering the
scale, you silently restyle every base component on the site. There's a test guarding against it —
don't fight it, use `textStyle`.

**The 22 available text styles:**

`heading1Strong` `heading1` `heading2` `heading3` · `body1Strong` `body1` `body2Strong` `body2` ·
`mobileBody1Strong` `mobileBody1` `mobileBody2` · `label` `caption` · `linkLg` `linkSm` ·
`button` `buttonSm` · `productNames` `price` · `navigation` · `footer` · `serif`

Browse them rendered in Storybook under **Foundation → Typography**.

### Colour — use the semantic aliases

```tsx
<Box bg="background.01" color="text.default" borderColor="border.default" />   // ✅
<Box bg="#f9f8f6" color="#191919" />                                          // ❌
```

Two layers exist. Reach for the **semantic** layer; the primitives are what the semantics are built from.

| Group | Keys |
|---|---|
| `text.*` | `default` `inverse` `inverseGrey` `secondary` `muted` |
| `background.*` | `01`–`07` (`01`–`04` light/ivory, `05`–`06` dark, `07` white) |
| `border.*` | `default` `secondary` `focus` `forms` `error` |
| `status.*` | `success` `error` `errorBackground` `storeClosed` |
| `link.*` · `icon.*` | `default` `hover` · `default` |
| `action.primary.*` | `bgDefault` `bgHover` `bgPressed` `bgDisabled` `bgFocused` `text` `textDisabled` |
| `action.secondary.*` | `border` `bgHover` `text` `textInverse` `textDisabled` |
| Primitives | `grey.{black,900,800,700,600,500,300,200,100,white}` `ivory.{100..400}` `coral/green/orange/red.500` `opacity.{15,30,40,50}` |

Browse under **Foundation → Colour**.

### Spacing

Both scales work — Chakra's numerics are preserved and the Zimmermann named scale is added on top.
**Prefer the named scale**, since it's what the design system speaks:

```tsx
<Box padding="m" marginBottom="xl" />   // ✅ 1rem, 1.5rem
<Box padding={4} />                      // works, but not the design vocabulary
```

`3xs` 0.125 · `2xs` 0.25 · `xs` 0.5 · `s` 0.75 · `m` 1 · `l` 1.25 · `xl` 1.5 · `2xl` 2 · `3xl` 2.5 ·
`4xl` 4 · `5xl` 5 · `6xl` 8 · `7xl` 10 — **in `rem`**, i.e. 2/4/8/12/16/20/24/32/40/64/80/128/160px at
the default 16px root font-size.

**The scale is `rem`, not `px`** — spacing and type scale with the user's root font-size and browser
zoom (WCAG 1.4.4). Hairline geometry deliberately does not:

- `borderWidth="default"` → `1px`, registered as a Chakra scale
- `focusRingOffsets.{default, secondary}` → `2px` / `3px`, imported as a constant from
  `app/theme/foundation` (`secondary` exists to clear the secondary button's 1px border)

**Unit rule:** `rem` for anything that should scale (type, spacing) · `px` only for hairline geometry
(border widths, focus-ring offsets) · `em` only for breakpoints. Never a raw literal of any unit in a
component file.

⚠️ **Don't use the `--zimm-scale-NNN` numeric aliases in JSX.** You'll see them in `zimmTokens.ts`
(`--zimm-scale-500`, `--zimm-scale-1100`, …). They exist **only** so the `.zimm-*` global classes have
something to reference. The named scale is the Chakra-facing surface:

```tsx
<Box mb="var(--zimm-scale-500)" />   // ❌ 20px, but bypasses the scale
<Box mb="l" />                        // ✅ same 20px, traceable to the token
```

If the value you need has no named entry — 28px and 44px are both in use with nothing between `xl` (24)
and `2xl` (32), or `3xl` (40) and `4xl` (64) — that's a **token gap to raise** (§7), not a reason to reach
for the numeric alias.

### Icon sizes, action sizes and motion are NOT theme tokens

These collide with Chakra scales too (`theme.sizes.lg` is 32rem and backs `w`/`h`/`boxSize` everywhere),
so they're **imported as constants** instead:

```tsx
import { iconSizes, actionSizes, motion } from 'app/theme/foundation';

<Icon boxSize={iconSizes.lg} />                                    // 20px
<Button height={actionSizes.height.lg} />                          // 52px
transition: `opacity ${motion.duration.fast} ${motion.easing.standard}`
```

`iconSizes` — `lg` 20 · `md` 16 · `sm` 12
`actionSizes` — `height.{lg:52, md:40}` · `paddingX.{lg:32, md:20}` · `gap:16`
`motion` — `duration.{fast:200ms, default:300ms, slow:500ms}` · `easing.{standard, slides, fades}`

⚠️ **Motion values are PROVISIONAL** and pending designer sign-off. Use them, but expect them to move.

#### The trap: a spacing token key on a sizing prop

This one shipped a completely broken footer, so it's worth being blunt about.

**`width` / `height` / `boxSize` / `min|maxWidth` / `min|maxHeight` resolve through `theme.sizes`.
`margin` / `padding` / `gap` / `top`-`right`-`bottom`-`left` resolve through `theme.space`.**

The Zimmermann named scale (`xs`, `m`, `l`, `xl`, `2xl`…) is registered as **`space` only** — deliberately,
for the collision reason above. So a scale key on a *sizing* prop falls through to **Chakra's default
`sizes`**, which reuses the same names for completely different values:

```tsx
// theme/components/footer.ts — intended a 24px icon touch target
width: 'xl',    // ❌ → var(--chakra-sizes-xl) = 36rem = 576px
height: 'xl',   // ❌   every contact icon became 576px; the footer layout collapsed on every page

width: 'var(--zimm-scale-xl)',   // ✅ 1.5rem = 24px — literal CSS, no scale lookup
```

Chakra's `sizes` are container widths: `xs` 20rem · `sm` 24rem · `md` 28rem · `lg` 32rem · `xl` 36rem.
Each is a plausible-looking, silent 20–30× blow-up.

**The rule:** on a sizing property use `var(--zimm-scale-*)`, an imported constant (`iconSizes`,
`actionSizes`), or an explicit unit — **never a bare scale key**. Bare keys are safe on spacing
properties only.

Nothing catches this. `'xl'` is a valid `SystemStyleObject` value so TypeScript is satisfied, no lint rule
exists, and no test asserts layout. It passed `tsc`, `eslint`, `vitest`, CodeRabbit (local *and* PR) and
the Storybook a11y run — only rendering the page found it.

#### Four more layout traps, all found by rendering rather than by any tool

**A shorthand resets a longhand you declared above it — in your own recipe.** The note above about not
introducing a shorthand where the *base* sets longhands has a sibling: order matters inside your own
object too.

```ts
paddingBlock: '4.5px',
// …twelve lines later…
padding: 0,          // ← silently wipes paddingBlock
```

The first attempt at the footer nav item had exactly this and appeared to do nothing at all. Use
`paddingInline: 0` when you mean "no horizontal padding". `recipeGuards.test.ts` catches a bare scale key
*inside* a shorthand; it does not catch this.

**A wrapped element takes the width available to it, not the width of its longest line.** The footer's
ABOUT column sat at its 160px cap while its longest rendered line was 115px — 45px of dead space that
pushed the next column right. `width: min-content` resolves to the widest *unbreakable run*, which is
what you want — but only for a label whose break is deliberate. On a single-line label it collapses to
the longest word and wraps it. Gate it on a signal that means "this break is intentional".

**Height from `minHeight` + `align-items: center` breaks the moment content wraps.** Centring only
distributes what a single line leaves over. A two-line label overflows the floor, so the leading
collapses to zero and the item sits flush against the one above. Derive height from `lineHeight` plus
padding instead — it holds at any line count.

**A block `<li>` wrapping an `inline-flex` `<a>` leaks ~1.5px per row.** The line box's strut adds
descender space below the baseline. Five rows cost 9px against Figma. `display: flex` on the list item
removes the line box entirely; axe confirmed list semantics survive.

#### Figma's text boxes are cap-height. Browser line boxes are not.

Figma reports a single-line footer item as 8px of text and two lines as 22px; the same text in a browser
measures ~14.5px and ~29px. **Transfer the rule, not the numbers.** For the nav item the rule was "equal
space above and below, height follows the line count" — expressed in our units as `lineHeight: 14px` plus
4.5px block padding, which lands on Figma's 24px and 38px exactly. Copying 8/22 would have produced
nonsense.

#### Type metrics change layout decisions — get the real font in first

Before the real faces were served, the fallback stack rendered roughly **13% wider**. Several sizing
decisions taken against it were simply wrong and had to be redone: a nav-column cap chosen to make one
label wrap stopped working once labels shrank, and a 768px overflow disappeared on its own. If a build
depends on measured text, self-host the font before you start measuring.

#### When no single value satisfies two constraints, constrain the text instead

The ACK label needed to wrap after the first word while "BOOK AN APPOINTMENT" stayed on one line. The
viable column cap was **[131, 132.9) — 1.9px**, a coincidence rather than a tolerance. A non-breaking
space between the words that must stay together widened the safe window to 71px. Content-level fixes are
sometimes the robust ones — but note the dependency: production copy has to carry the same character.

### The `.zimm-*` global classes — and the one rule about them

**27** global classes exist: `.zimm-text-*` (typography), `.zimm-form-*` (form-field layout),
`.zimm-grid`, `.zimm-focus-visible`. They mirror the design system as static CSS so handover markup can
be pasted and look right. They are **not** the preferred authoring route for new Zimmermann components —
default to the hierarchy above.

**There are no `.zimm-btn-*` classes, and there must never be.** The whole family was deleted
deliberately, and the reason generalises:

> **One canonical styling surface per component type.** If a component has interactive state, its
> `theme/components/<name>.ts` recipe is the only place its look is defined. A static CSS class cannot
> express `_hover` / `_active` / `_disabled` / `_focusVisible`, so a class "mirror" of a recipe is
> structurally incomplete from birth — and nothing stops the two drifting apart afterwards.

So: **every button is Chakra's `<Button>` styled by `theme/components/button.ts`.** Never a class, never
a hand-rolled `<button>` with its own styles. `.zimm-*` classes remain the right tool only for genuinely
static, non-interactive, heavily-reused treatments — typography, the grid, form-field layout.

⚠️ Worth knowing: `globalStyles.ts` has almost no consumers today (one Storybook demo uses `.zimm-grid`)
and it ships on every page. Don't reach for a class where a prop or a recipe will do.

### Interaction state goes in CSS, never in React state

This is the rule most likely to cost you a rewrite, so it's worth being blunt about.

Hover, press, focus and disabled belong in the component's theme recipe as Chakra's pseudo-props. They do
**not** belong in `useState`.

```tsx
// ❌ never — interaction state in React
const [hovered, setHovered] = useState(false)
<button onMouseEnter={() => setHovered(true)} style={{background: hovered ? a : b}}>

// ✅ theme/components/myThing.ts — the browser does the work
_hover:        { bg: 'var(--zimm-color-action-primary-bg-hover)' },
_active:       { bg: 'var(--zimm-color-action-primary-bg-pressed)' },
_disabled:     { bg: 'var(--zimm-color-border-secondary)', cursor: 'not-allowed' },
_focusVisible: { outline: 'var(--zimm-focus-ring)', outlineOffset: 'var(--zimm-focus-ring-offset-default)' },
```

It looks identical in a screenshot. It behaves differently in five ways that all matter here:

| JS state | CSS pseudo-class |
|---|---|
| Dead until hydration — the button renders but doesn't respond | Works on first paint, no JS needed |
| No way to express `@media (hover: hover)` → sticky hover on touch after a tap | Opts out on touch devices properly |
| Inline styles win every specificity fight — the theme **cannot** override them | Overridable by variant, later |
| The keyboard focus ring built for WCAG 2.4.7 lives in the recipe, so it never applies | Inherited automatically |
| Every hover re-renders the component | No React work at all |

With a ≤2s p75 mobile LCP budget and a WCAG 2.2 AA target, the first and fourth rows are the ones that
turn into defects.

**Corollary — a theme recipe nothing consumes is dead code.** If you write
`theme/components/myThing.ts` and register it, the component has to actually read it — Chakra's
`<Button>`/`<Link>` etc. do so automatically; a custom multipart component needs
`useStyleConfig('MyThing')`. A registered-but-unread recipe looks like compliance and changes nothing.

### The styling surface for a ui-kit component — decided

**A theme recipe, always.** Not inline styles, not a `.zimm-*` class, not a co-located CSS file. Pick the
case that matches what you're building:

| Case | What you write |
|---|---|
| It **is** a Chakra component (`Button`, `Link`, `Input`) | A recipe at `theme/components/<name>.ts`. Chakra resolves `variant`/`size` automatically — your component is a thin prop-mapping layer |
| A **bespoke multipart** Zimmermann component | A recipe + register it + read it with `useMultiStyleConfig` + build on the `chakra()` factory |
| Genuinely **static, non-interactive, heavily reused** | A `.zimm-*` class in `globalStyles.ts` |
| Nothing above fits | `sx`, then a co-located `.scss` — last resort, per `css.md` |

**The bespoke case, worked** — this is the one people get stuck on, because a recipe can't style a bare
`<input>`. The `chakra()` factory is the bridge: it makes a native element theme-aware, so you keep native
semantics *and* get recipe styling.

```ts
// theme/components/zimmTextInput.ts
import type { SystemStyleObject } from '@chakra-ui/react';
// Figma node 40000265:374 — field/border/* tokens
const BORDER = { default: 'var(--zimm-color-border-forms)', … } as const;
export const ZimmTextInput = { parts: [...], baseStyle: {...}, variants: {...} };
```
```ts
// theme/components/index.ts — register it, or destructuring throws at runtime
export const components = { Button, Footer, Header, ListMenu, ZimmNavItem, ZimmTextInput };
```
```tsx
// components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmTextInput/index.tsx
import { chakra, useMultiStyleConfig } from '@chakra-ui/react';
const styles = useMultiStyleConfig('ZimmTextInput', { inverse, disabled });
```

Note the theme key is **PascalCase** (`ZimmTextInput`) while the file is camelCase
(`zimmTextInput.ts`) — the key is the Chakra component name, the filename follows our convention. Same
split as `listMenu.ts` → `ListMenu`.

**Why not co-located CSS, when plain CSS handles `:hover` perfectly well?** Because a stylesheet can only
see `var(--zimm-*)`, and those are **derived output** — the bottom of the token pipeline. Author there and
you give up `textStyle`, the named `theme.space` scale, semantic colour tokens, responsive arrays, and the
125 drift-guard tests in `theme/index.test.tsx`. It isn't bad CSS; it's the wrong end of the pipeline.

*(You may see `.styles.ts` files using `.zimm-*` classes on the F2R conversion branch. They're a faithful
Figma→CSS transcription and excellent raw material for writing a recipe — convert them, don't copy the
pattern. `.zimm-btn-*` classes in particular were deliberately removed from `globalStyles.ts`; don't
reintroduce them anywhere.)*

### Adding a new token

**You don't.** `overrides/app/theme/foundation/` is Tier 1 and designer-owned (Hard Rule #3). If Figma
has a value with no token, that's a §7 escalation, not a local addition. Same for
`theme/globalStyles.ts` (Tier 2, needs a named owner's nod).

Per-component theme overrides in `theme/components/` **are** yours to add — one file per Chakra
component, registered in `theme/components/index.ts`.

### Naming a recipe — `extendTheme` MERGES, it does not replace

`theme/index.ts` composes with `extendTheme(baseTheme, overrides)`, and that is a **deep merge**. If your
recipe key matches an SFCC base recipe key, you are not replacing theirs — **you are inheriting it.**

Base SFCC ships recipes for `Footer`, `Header`, `ListMenu`, `Button`, `CheckoutFooter` and more. Register
a recipe called `Footer` and every part name you happen to share silently inherits the base's properties.

Two failure modes, both seen on this project:

**1 · Properties you never chose.** SFCC's `Footer.copyright` is `{fontSize: 'sm', marginBottom: 6}`. Our
recipe set `textStyle: 'footer'` (10px) — the base's literal `fontSize: 'sm'` won, so copyright rendered
at **14px with a stray 24px bottom margin** nobody wrote.

**2 · Reordered output — the dangerous one.** A key that already exists in the base keeps the *base's*
position in the merged object; a key you add that the base lacks is appended **last**. So:

```ts
// ours
subscribeHeading: { margin: 0, /* … */ marginBottom: 'xl' }   // 24px gap intended
```
```css
/* merged output — base already had marginBottom, so ours took its early slot;
   `margin` was new, so it landed last and reset the shorthand */
margin-bottom: var(--chakra-space-xl);   /* 24px */
margin: 0px;                             /* ← wins. Gap is now 0. */
```

In isolation Chakra emits these in the correct order. **Only the merge inverts them.**

**The rule:**

- **Full rewrite** (your recipe shares almost nothing with the base) → **namespace the key**:
  `ZimmFooter`, not `Footer`, consumed as `useMultiStyleConfig('ZimmFooter')`. Same convention
  `ZimmNavItem` and `ZimmTextInput` already follow.
- **Genuine partial override** (you want the base's other parts — `Header`, `ListMenu`, `Button`) → keep
  the base key, but **never introduce a CSS shorthand on a part where the base sets longhands.** Your
  `margin`/`padding`/`background`/`border` is appended last and will wipe them.
- Always declare your own `parts` array. A recipe with no `parts` inherits the base's list, so any
  Zimmermann part you add is undeclared.

To see exactly what you're inheriting, diff the merged recipe against your source:

```js
theme.components.Header.baseStyle   // merged — what actually applies
```

## 4. The build sequence

Four steps, in order. This is the agreed approach.

### Step 1 — Does it already exist?

§2. Check the registry and the base package. Report what you found in the PR description, even when the
answer is "nothing" — that's the evidence the ladder was walked.

### Step 2 — Use as-is, override/extend, or build custom?

| Verdict | When | What you do |
|---|---|---|
| **Use as-is** | Base behaviour and markup are right; only styling differs | Style it via `theme/components/<name>.ts`. No component file at all |
| **Override / extend** | Base structure is right, behaviour or markup needs changing | Copy-first (§2), then modify. **Minimal changes** — don't remove base functionality you weren't asked to touch |
| **Build custom** | Nothing upstream is close | `/new-component` scaffolds it. Justify the call in the PR |

Most work should land in the first two columns. If you're reaching for "custom" often, raise it — either
the ladder isn't being walked or there's a real gap worth naming.

**If SFCC's own components import the thing you're overriding, use the bridge pattern.** Check first:

```bash
grep -r "from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/<name>'" \
  node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/
```

Any hits mean base components depend on it, so its **default export must stay a faithful, undecorated
port** — full original prop surface, same `forwardRef` behaviour. Put Zimmermann-only styling behind a
**named export** that wraps the default. Get this wrong and you restyle or break base cart / checkout /
account screens you never opened.

Where the brand difference is purely token-driven you don't need the split at all — put it in
`theme/components/<name>.ts` instead, and leave the default export untouched.

⚠️ **No worked precedent exists in the repo yet.** `overrideStyling.md` describes this pattern using
`product-tile` (`CardBaseline` + faithful default), `link`, `image-gallery`, `display-price` and
`swatch-group` — **none of which are overrides on `develop` today.** The pattern is the agreed approach;
you may well be the one who establishes the first example of it. If you are, say so in the PR so the rule
file can be updated to point at something real.

### Step 3 — Execute the swap / override / build

Component folder layout (`.claude/rules/conventions.md`):

```
overrides/app/components/productTile/
  index.tsx            ← the component (named export matching the folder)
  index.stories.tsx    ← mandatory
  index.test.ts        ← only if logic-heavy
  types.ts             ← only if props are shared with siblings
  productTile.scss     ← only if Chakra props genuinely can't express it
```

- **Zimmermann-authored files:** `camelCase` (`productTile.tsx`)
- **Override files mirroring a base file:** keep the original kebab-case exactly (`product-tile.tsx`)
- **TypeScript only inside `overrides/`.** No `.js`/`.jsx`, including stories and config
- Named export matches the folder; props type is `<ComponentName>Props`
- Callbacks are `onEventName`; required props non-optional, optional props use `?`
- Australian spelling in Zimmermann-authored code (`colour`, `centre`) — override files keep upstream
  spelling verbatim
- No magic numbers or strings — name the constant
- JSDoc required on anything with ≥2 callers and on every exported hook

**Split it up when:** the component passes ~150 lines, branches heavily, or accumulates ≥2 related
`useState` calls (→ extract a hook in `overrides/app/hooks/use<Component><Feature>.ts`).

### Step 4 — Apply the design styles

§3. Chakra props first, tokens always, `textStyle` for type. Then check it against Figma at the
breakpoints the design defines, and raise what doesn't line up.

## 5. Storybook — non-negotiable, and your build surface

Every component exported from its folder needs a `*.stories.tsx`. Internal sub-components that only
render inside one parent don't — cover their variants through the parent.

Build **in** Storybook rather than building and then adding a story. It's the fastest loop you have,
and it's the only place a reviewer can see every state at once.

```bash
npm run storybook
```

**Two things Storybook will not show you truthfully.**

Base-template SVGs are `ignore-loader`ed in `.storybook/main.js`, mirroring the browser build. Any icon
sourced from `@salesforce/retail-react-app` therefore renders as an **empty box** in Storybook while
rendering correctly in the app. Twelve of `ZimmIcon`'s types are currently in that state. Our own icons
in `zimm.tsx` are unaffected — so an icon that appears blank in Storybook is usually a sourcing signal,
not a broken glyph.

`test-storybook` needs a **built** Storybook (`build-storybook` + a static server), which is what CI does.
Pointing it at a running dev server produces wholesale failures that mean nothing.

**Categorisation** (drives the sidebar; pick the first that matches):

| Category | What goes here |
|---|---|
| `Foundation/` | Design tokens — Colour, Typography, Spacing, Icons |
| `Elements/` | Generic building blocks — Button, Input, Badge, Link, Checkbox. *Tiebreaker: usable outside a form?* → `Elements/` |
| `Layout/` | Global chrome and structure — Header, Footer, DrawerMenu, Breadcrumb, Pagination |
| `Commerce/` | Commerce-specific shared — ProductTile, OrderSummary, PromoCode, DisplayPrice |
| `Forms/` | Composed form assemblies — AddressForm, NewsletterSignup |
| `Pages/` | Full page assemblies |
| `Contentful/` | CMS-driven — use mock Contentful data so variants are visible without a live CMS |

```ts
export default { title: 'Commerce/ProductTile' };   // ✅
export default { title: 'Elements/DisplayPrice' };  // ❌ commerce-specific → Commerce/
```

**Content:** every file has a `Default` export. Add named exports for meaningful states (`Loading`,
`OutOfStock`, `WithDiscount`, `Empty`) — not for every prop permutation. This is where your static-first
data lives.

**`play` functions** only where there's interactive behaviour worth asserting — validation on blur,
disclosure open/close, focus movement. Query through `within(canvasElement)`, prefer `getByRole` with
an accessible name, and import `userEvent` from `@storybook/test` (not `@testing-library/user-event`).

⚠️ **If a component looks wrong in Storybook but right in the app, suspect your imports before your
CSS.** `--zimm-*` variables now resolve correctly in Storybook (§3 trap 1). The likely cause is §3 trap
1b: a base-path import of an already-overridden component renders the *base* SFCC version in Storybook
and Vitest while working fine in the app. Switch it to a relative import.

### Your branch gets a live URL, automatically

Separate from Storybook, and new: every push to a `feature/*` or `fix/*` branch now builds and deploys
itself to its own dedicated MRT environment, then posts the URL as a comment on the PR.

- Created on first push and **reused** on later pushes — one environment per branch, not per commit. The
  comment updates in place rather than piling up.
- **Torn down automatically** when the PR closes or the branch is deleted.
- A real Sydney-hosted (`ap-southeast-2`) storefront with real dev environment variables — not a mock.
- Excluded: `fix/release-*` sub-branches and `hotfix/*`.

Use it for design review, QA sign-off, and anything cross-device. Nobody needs your branch checked out
locally to look at your work, and it's why you should never have to fight over the shared dev target
again.

Storybook is still where you **build** — fastest loop, every state visible at once. The preview
environment is where other people **review**.

## 6. Accessibility — written as AC, not added later

Baseline is **WCAG 2.2 AA**. Fall back to 2.1 AA only where 2.2 is technically infeasible, and document
why in the story.

### The standing set — apply to every component

- Keyboard operability and reachability
- Focus order, and a **visible** focus state
- All interaction states: hover, active, disabled, focused
- Screen-reader behaviour for images and icon-only controls
- Behaviour when optional content is absent (no empty box, no layout break)
- Target size ≥ 24×24 CSS px for interactive controls (SC 2.5.8)

### Already mechanically enforced — you'll be caught anyway

| Check | By |
|---|---|
| `<img>` without `alt` (`alt=""` is fine when decorative) | ast-grep |
| `IconButton` / `IconButtonWithRegistration` without `aria-label` | ast-grep |
| `onClick` on a non-interactive element without `role` | ast-grep |
| Unsanitised `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` | semgrep |
| Storybook a11y violations | `@storybook/addon-a11y`, `test: 'error'` — **fails CI** |

⚠️ **The `<img>` rule matches lowercase `<img>` only.** Chakra's `<Image>` is *not* covered. Most
components here use `<Image>` — that one is on you.

### Not enforced anywhere — genuinely your responsibility

Keyboard flow, focus order, colour-contrast in states, screen-reader semantics beyond the above, and
whether the disabled state is actually communicated rather than just faded.

## 7. When you find a gap

You will find them. Figma will be missing a state, a token won't exist, a requirement will contradict
itself. **Raise, don't invent.**

| What you found | Where it goes |
|---|---|
| Value in Figma with no token | Design review (Kiera) via the lead — never add to `foundation/` yourself |
| Missing design for a state (hover/disabled/error/empty) | Design review, and flag on the story before it's sized |
| Design contradicts a signed-off PRD in `.docs/prd/` | **Stop.** Cite doc + section + requirement ID, ask which wins. Don't proceed silently either way |
| Requirement unclear, ambiguous, or unconfirmed | Ask in the group chat first; if it changes scope, it goes back to refinement |
| Contrast/a11y failure in the tokens themselves | Raise with the lead — several are already known (§3) |
| Needs a new npm package | **Stop.** Integration team approval required. Check `package.json` first — something installed may already do it |
| Needs a shared hook's signature changed | **Stop.** Team RFC |
| Touches a Tier 1 file | **Stop.** See `.claude/rules/frozenFiles.md` |

Ask **one question at a time** and wait for the answer — batching them gets them half-answered.

---

## 8. Before you open a PR

**Green locally before you open it.** Not a nicety — a PR that doesn't compile spends a reviewer's whole
budget on nothing, and review here runs an hour or more per UI PR.

```bash
npx tsc --noEmit          # must be clean
npm run lint              # must not add new errors
npm test                  # Vitest
npm run build-storybook && npx test-storybook   # play functions + a11y — Vitest does NOT cover these
/code-quality             # naming, imports, structure, missing stories/tests
```

**Vitest does not run `play` functions.** A change that breaks a story passes `npm test` and fails in CI.
That happened on the footer PR: making a text-input control opt-in removed a button a `play` function
clicked, `tsc`/`lint`/`vitest` were all green, and CI caught it at 1 failure in 73.

Two failure modes specific to this repo, both seen already:

- **A `develop` merge can silently delete a type declaration.** If your branch added something to
  `overrides/app/types/vendor.d.ts` and `develop` also changed that file, the merge can resolve to
  develop's version and drop yours. Re-run `tsc` **after** every merge from `develop`, not just before.
- **Sometimes the rule is wrong, not your code.** One recent failure came from following a repo rules file
  that named a package which doesn't exist on the installed Storybook major. If a documented import
  doesn't resolve, check the package actually exists before assuming you mistyped it — then flag the rule.

### Self-review across the same three surfaces the reviewer will use

Cheaper to catch it yourself than in a review round-trip:

| Surface | What you're checking |
|---|---|
| **The diff** | Correct tokens in the correct layer, reuse over reimplementation, no raw literals |
| **The preview environment** | What it actually renders — every state, every breakpoint, hover and focus genuinely working |
| **Figma, side by side** | Parity at the breakpoints the design defines |

Your branch's preview URL is posted on the PR automatically (§5). If a difference from Figma is a *design*
gap rather than a build gap, say so in the PR description — don't quietly resolve it.

Then a local CodeRabbit review — **required, not optional**:

```bash
coderabbit auth status && cr review --light --base develop
```

If the CLI isn't installed or authenticated, install it (coderabbit.ai/cli) and run
`npm run env -- init` for the shared key rather than committing without a review. The GitHub PR review
is still the real gate; this one catches things earlier.

### Self-check

- [ ] Ladder walked — reuse checked and reported, "custom" justified
- [ ] Copy-first done and confirmed if `Origin = Base`; `console.log` markers removed
- [ ] All design values are tokens — **no hardcoded hex, no raw px/rem/em** (still not mechanically
      enforced: `overrideStyling.md` points at `scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs`, which does not exist yet —
      so this stays the highest-frequency violation in review)
- [ ] Type set with `textStyle`, never `fontSize`
- [ ] Storybook story exists, categorised correctly, `Default` plus meaningful states
- [ ] Vitest where logic is non-obvious — data mapping, transforms, complex state
- [ ] Accessibility AC met, including the parts no tool checks
- [ ] Optional/absent content handled — no empty space, no layout break
- [ ] No data-fetching hooks inside a `components/` file
- [ ] No `console.log`/`console.error` left behind
- [ ] Existing comments and commented-out code left alone (only remove alongside the code they describe)
- [ ] One protection tier touched, not several
- [ ] `/pr-checklist` run to generate the description

**Commits, pushes and PRs happen only when explicitly asked.** Finishing the work is not the trigger.

---

## 9. Hard stops

Non-negotiable. From AGENTS.md.

- **Never work on `develop` or `main`.**
- **Never modify `overrides/app/theme/foundation/`** — designer-owned.
- **Never modify** `overrides/app/ssr.js`, `config/default.js`, `config/sites.js`, `worker/main.js` —
  absolute, no approver exception.
- **Never modify test config** — `vitest.config.*`, `playwright.config.*`, `.storybook/`, `lighthouserc.js`.
- **Never add or remove packages** without integration-team approval. Use `npm install`, don't hand-edit
  `package.json`.
- **Never delete files** unless explicitly asked. Propose it and let a human confirm.
- **Never refactor upward** — fixing a component doesn't license changing the hook it calls.
- **Never rename or move a shared hook or component.**
- **Never reference a later sprint's code** — check `.docs/memory/sprintScope.md`.
- **Never run `npm start`** — ask; the dev server is shared.
- **Never load a third-party script outside a Didomi consent callback.** Fail closed: unknown consent
  state means load nothing.

### Shared-shell coordination

`header/` `footer/` `drawer-menu/` `list-menu/` `seo/` `_app/` `_app-config/` `routes.tsx` are Tier 2
shared shell — **coordinate with the other squad before touching.** Same for
`product-tile/` `product-item/` `display-price/` `image-gallery/` `swatch-group/` (Squad B owns) and
`order-summary/` `promo-code/` `pickup-or-delivery/` (Squad A owns).

---

## 10. Performance — it's a requirement, not a polish pass

Mobile page speed is a top project priority. **LCP budget ≤ 2s at p75 mobile.**

- **Images:** always lazy-load, always serve correctly sized. Never render a full-res image at thumbnail size.
- **Code splitting:** dynamic `import()` for heavy components not needed on first render.
- **Data fetching:** request only the fields you need. No waterfalls — parallelise.
- **Third-party scripts:** must not block LCP. `defer`/`async`/post-hydration only, and always behind Didomi.
- **Bundle size:** gated at `main.js` ≤ 180 kB, `vendor.js` ≤ 550 kB. Don't introduce a large dependency
  without asking. *(Note: there is currently no CSS budget in CI — that doesn't mean CSS is free.)*

---

## 11. Quick reference

### Commands

```bash
/session-start                    # start-of-session ritual
/audit-tier <path>                # tier, owner, blast radius
/scope-check                      # is this prompt safe to run
/new-component                     # scaffold component + story
/code-quality                     # audit before PR
/pr-checklist                     # generate PR description
npx tsc --noEmit                  # type check
npm run lint                      # ESLint
npm test                          # Vitest
npm run storybook                 # Storybook at :6006
cr review --light --base develop  # local CodeRabbit
```

### Paths

| What | Where |
|---|---|
| Components | `overrides/app/components/` |
| Hooks | `overrides/app/hooks/` |
| Pages | `overrides/app/pages/` |
| Shared types | `overrides/app/types/{commerce,components,hooks}.ts` |
| Design tokens (Tier 1, read-only) | `overrides/app/theme/foundation/` |
| Component theme overrides (yours) | `overrides/app/theme/components/` |
| **Styling rules — canonical, read this** | `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md` |
| `--zimm-*` injection (app + Storybook) | `overrides/app/theme/zimmTokensGlobal.tsx` |
| Icons — **single source of truth** | `overrides/app/components/icons/` |
| Registries | `.claude/registry/*.md` |
| Rules | `.claude/rules/*.md` |
| Requirements | `.docs/prd/` · integrations `.docs/integration/NN-*.md` |

**Icons:** import only from `overrides/app/components/icons`. Never from
`@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/icons`. If an icon is missing, **ask** — don't substitute
a visually different one.

### The eight things people get wrong most

1. **Interaction state in `useState` instead of the recipe's `_hover` / `_active` / `_focusVisible`** →
   identical in a screenshot; dead until hydration, sticky on touch, and unstylable by the theme (§3)
2. `fontSize="md"` instead of `textStyle` → wrong size, silently
3. **A spacing scale key on a sizing prop** — `width: 'xl'` → `theme.sizes.xl` = **36rem**, not
   `space.xl` = 1.5rem. A silent 24× blow-up that no tool catches. Use `var(--zimm-scale-*)` (§3)
4. **Naming a recipe after an SFCC base recipe** — `extendTheme` merges, so `Footer` inherits SFCC's
   `Footer`, and any shorthand you add lands last and wipes the base's longhands. Namespace it
   (`ZimmFooter`) for a rewrite (§3)
5. Importing an already-overridden component by its `@salesforce/...` base path → your story or test
   silently exercises the unstyled **base** component while the app renders fine (§3 trap 1b)
6. A hardcoded hex or px that "matched the design" → no tool catches it; review will. Reaching for a
   `--zimm-scale-NNN` alias instead of the named scale counts as the same mistake
7. Data-fetching inside a `components/` file → makes the later integration a rewrite
8. Skipping copy-first on an `Origin = Base` component → the override never renders and you debug the
   wrong file

**3 and 4 are the two that a screenshot won't reveal and a reviewer won't spot in a diff** — both were
found on SFCC-55 only by rendering the page and measuring it. They are the strongest argument for the
three-surface self-review in §8.

---

`.zimm-*` classes, the 125 theme guard tests, the three registered recipes, every colour group and key,
`iconSizes` / `actionSizes` / `motion`, `BTN_HEIGHT_LG`/`SM`/`BTN_PADDING_Y`, `NAV_LETTER_SPACING`,
`FONT_SERIF`, `--zimm-scale-500 = spacing.l`, the bundlesize budgets, and all six npm scripts. Corrected in

actually overridden today" in §2.*

# SFCC-89 / PR #57 — Consolidated Findings

Investigation date: 2026-08-22. Repo: `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa`.
Branch: `feature/SFCC-89_pdp-ui-static-product-information` @ `d526ad1`.

This is the authoritative summary. Five deeper reports sit alongside it in the same folder:
`req-jira.md`, `req-figma.md`, `code-state.md`, `pr57-review.md`, `conventions.md`, plus
`pr57-body.md` (the PR description verbatim).

---

## 0. Situation

We are **taking over an in-flight PR authored by someone else**. PR #57
"feat(pdp): SFCC-89 — PDP UI static product information", author **JhoanDelaCruz**,
opened 2026-08-18, last pushed 2026-08-21. 24 commits, +1702/−99 across 30 files.
Base `develop`. State OPEN / `CHANGES_REQUESTED` / `MERGEABLE` / `BLOCKED`.
0 commits behind develop.

The four scope decisions (page composition, ticket ownership, sanitiser, PR strategy)
have been **deliberately deferred by the FED Lead**. Work continues on the existing
branch for now. No code has been changed. No commits. No pushes.

---

## 1. What SFCC-89 asks for

Story, High, 5 points, Sprint 3 (10–24 Aug), status **Code Review**, assignee Jhoan
Rose Dela Cruz, reporter Jasmijn Tsang, due 17 Aug (overdue). Parent epic **SFCC-5
(PDP)** — a Level 2 *page* epic.

**The acceptance criteria are in a custom field (`customfield_10231`), not the
description** — easy to miss entirely. Six Given/When/Then items:

1. Product name
2. Price — single full price, in storefront currency
3. Description
4. Style code
5. Model copy ("Model is…"), including the negative case (no empty placeholder)
6. Breadcrumb beneath the product images: `HOME / NEW / DRESSES / [PRODUCT NAME]`,
   nodes navigate to category

Two further styling ACs live in standalone Tasks **SFCC-732 / SFCC-733** (both To Do),
citing Figma node `5804-170721`. They assert `.product-name` / `.product-price` CSS
selectors that **the component does not expose** — values match, selectors do not, so
they fail at QA as written.

**Explicitly out of scope**, with owning tickets: badges (SFCC-132/225), was/now pricing
(SFCC-194), wishlist (SFCC-434), colour swatches (SFCC-91), size + add-to-bag (SFCC-92),
Find in Boutique (SFCC-297), image gallery (SFCC-186/187/188), accordions
(SFCC-195/102/267/266).

---

## 2. Findings ranked by severity

### P0-A — Merging this removes the storefront PDP

`overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx` (95 lines) replaces the base SFCC PDP
(876 lines). It renders exactly three things: an empty grey `<Box>` placeholder for the
gallery (`:56`), `<PdpProductInfo>` (`:74`), and the breadcrumb toolbar (`:85`).

Everything else in the base page disappears: `ProductView` (add-to-bag, swatches,
quantity picker), `RecommendedProducts`, `InformationAccordion`, `<Helmet>`/`<Seo>`,
`HTTPNotFound` 404 handling, SSR cache headers, `<Island>` hydration, and the full
`useProduct` expand list.

**Two independent shadowing mechanisms, so deleting the route entry does not fix it:**
1. `overrides/app/routes.tsx:37` registers `/product/:productId` before `..._routes`.
2. The override mirrors the base path exactly, so `ccExtensibility` redirects base
   `routes.jsx:43`'s own `import('./pages/product-detail')` to the override too.

Verified directly, not inferred. Nothing in the PR body acknowledges this.

### P0-B — The PDP throws on every SSR request, and the cause is the unapproved dependency

CI artifact shows, for every `/product/*` request, valid and invalid SKU alike:

```
ReferenceError: Cannot access '__WEBPACK_DEFAULT_EXPORT__' before initialization
    at Module.default (build/main-server.js:71360:42)
```

**Root cause established by direct inspection.** `isomorphic-dompurify`'s node entry
(`dist/index.mjs`) instantiates JSDOM at module-evaluation time:

```js
import { JSDOM } from "jsdom";
var window = new JSDOM("<!DOCTYPE html>").window;   // runs on import
var purify = DOMPurifyFactory(window);
```

`overrides/app/components/pdpProductInfo/index.tsx:2` imports it at module scope. Bundled
into `main-server.js`, jsdom's CommonJS interop produces `__WEBPACK_DEFAULT_EXPORT__`, and
the module-scope `new JSDOM()` executes before that binding initialises. Explains every
symptom: PDP-only, SKU-independent, homepage unaffected, and a *build* that succeeds
because this is an evaluation-order failure, not a compile error.

Consequence: Playwright went **0-for-7** on PDP scenarios (6 retries exhausted, 2 skipped)
then hit the 15-minute job timeout; `mobile-chrome` never ran; no HTML report produced.
**The PR body attributes these failures to missing sandbox products. That is not what is
happening.**

I ruled out a circular import in our own code: a value-import cycle scan across
`overrides/app` (110 modules reachable from the PDP entry, resolving base-package imports
through the override redirect) found **no cycles**. The only two hits were override files
importing their own base path, which is the documented PWA Kit self-reference pattern.

### P0-C — Tier 1 dependency added without approval

`package.json` gains `isomorphic-dompurify@^3.19.0` as a **production** dependency
(commit `0068e1a`). `package.json` is Tier 1 frozen; AGENTS.md Hard Rule #7 forbids adding
packages without Integration team approval. **The PR body itself states the approval is
needed and has not been obtained** — then the dependency was added anyway.

Context: the repo has only **four** production dependencies total. The lockfile shows the
install flipped a chain of jsdom-related packages (`@asamuzakjp/*` and others) from
`dev: true` into the production tree. 16 MB installed, jsdom ~12 MB.

Scope of the actual need is tiny: **two** `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` sites, both in
`pdpProductInfo/index.tsx` (`:43` description, `:54` model info). Nothing else in
`overrides/` uses it.

**Measured, not assumed:** I ran `npm run build`. It succeeds. Bundle budgets **pass** —
`main.js` 103.46 KB gzip (limit 180 KB), `vendor.js` 524.74 KB gzip (limit 550 KB).
Note vendor is at **95.4% of budget** with ~25 KB headroom. No circular-dependency warning
was emitted, but webpack does not emit those by default.

### P1 — Multi-tier change (Hard Rule #10)

- **Tier 1:** `package.json`, `package-lock.json`
- **Tier 2:** `routes.tsx`, `theme/components/index.ts`, `theme/components/pdpProductInfo.ts`
  (owner: **UI Designer** — not notified)
- Clean: `.github/workflows/`, `config/`, `.storybook/`, `theme/foundation/`, `ssr.js`,
  and every Tier 2 shared-product component.

The PR body's changed-files table lists **15 files and omits every Tier 1 file**. The real
diff is 30 files.

### P1 — Ownership contradiction between two governance files

- `CODEOWNERS:159` → `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/` → **`@ZimmermannAU/pwa-squad-b`**
- `.claude/rules/squadA.md` lists the same path as **Squad A** territory

CODEOWNERS is the enforcement surface, so GitHub will require a Squad B review regardless.
This PR also reclassifies ProductDetail to Squad A in the generated registry. Unresolved.

### P1 — Breadcrumb silently restyles the PLP

`overrides/app/components/breadcrumb/` shadows a **shared SFCC component** consumed by
`product-view/index.jsx:75` and `product-list/partials/page-header.jsx:20`. Effects:
chevron separator → `/`, theme config → hardcoded styles, `...rest` dropped, `categories`
made required. Violates the SFCC bridge-pattern rule in `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md`
(shared components must keep a faithful, undecorated default export; brand styling goes
behind a named export or a theme recipe).

*Ruled out:* a suspected locale-URL regression — base `categoryUrlBuilder` ignores its
locale argument, so the inlined copy is behaviourally identical.

### P1 — No human has reviewed this PR

All **8 reviews and all 22 inline threads are `coderabbitai[bot]`**. The
`CHANGES_REQUESTED` decision is entirely the bot's. Five reviewer teams were requested —
PWA Squad A, PWA Squad B, PWA QA, Tier-1 Approvers, Tier-2 Approvers — **none responded**.
The only human comments are the author's own note about a BrowserStack secret and
`marcelannavarro` typing `@coderabbitai full-review`.

---

## 3. Acceptance-criteria conformance

| AC | State | Gap |
|---|---|---|
| Product name | Built | `h1` has no `data-testid` while all four siblings do; SFCC-732 asserts `.product-name`, which does not exist |
| Price — single full price | Partial | Uses `product.price` (current price, not necessarily full). When `currency` is absent, renders `''` — an empty element that still occupies layout instead of being omitted |
| Description | Partial | `shortDescription \|\| longDescription` (`page:77`) is a guess; the AC does not say which field |
| Style code | **Wrong source** | Reads `product?.id` (`page:79`). SFCC-26 defines style code as the **master** ID / `styleNumber`. Latent until SFCC-91 adds colour-variant routing, then silently wrong |
| Model copy + negative case | **Wrong source** | Reads `c_sizeFit`, not the `modelFit` attribute SFCC-26 created specifically for this line. Jasmijn's comments confirm `modelFit` was deliberate. `sizeFit` belongs to the Size & Fit tab (SFCC-102, out of scope) |
| Breadcrumb | Partial | Leaf category omitted; no `BreadcrumbList` JSON-LD (the whole point of SFCC-578); `Home` hardcoded |

`extractModelLine` (`overrides/app/utils/productData.ts`) is:

```ts
const match = html.match(/<li>\s*(Model is[^<]*?)\s*<\/li>/i);
```

Two defects: matches only a **bare** `<li>` (any attribute breaks it), and matches only the
**English** string. Returns `undefined` on 10 of 11 locales.

---

## 4. Figma design spec

Design: `QQ427wHWEUjsjP7H8v48Rs` (composed page states), node `3087:15747`.
**Never cross-compare with `wPiWmZZOVKnrENUWk2XWWm` (the design system file).**

**Two corrections to the original brief:**
- `3087:15747` is a **PAGE**, not a screen — 67 children, 108649×41878 px.
- Only **402** and **1440** frames exist. **No 1023 frame. Tablet is undesigned.**
  Repo breakpoints are `md 768` / `xl 1280`; **no `860` token exists anywhere in the theme.**

**Tooling limits hit:** `get_variable_defs` and `get_design_context` resolve against the
Figma **desktop app's current selection** and ignore the `nodeId` argument — both returned
"You currently have nothing selected". Substituted read-only Plugin API traversal, which
gives resolved variable names/collections/modes rather than pre-rendered Tailwind.
`get_metadata` on the target fails deterministically (subtree >315 KB vs the SSE cap). A
non-ASCII character in some layer names breaks SSE encoding outright.

**Measurement rules applied.** TEXT nodes report a cap-height box, not comparable to a CSS
line box. FRAMES/INSTANCES report real boxes and are comparable. A **third case** was
found that the brief did not cover: **a FRAME that hugs a TEXT child inherits the
cap-height artifact** — accordion rows report `218x9`, which is text cap-height, not row
height (real pitch ≈ 25.5 px). Uniform residual = artifact; varying residual = defect.

### Matches
Seven text styles map exactly (`heading3`, `price`, `body2`, `caption`, `linkLg`,
`linkSm`, `button`), four colour tokens, spacing 2/4/8/16/24/30/80. The DS spacing scale
is **1:1 identical** to `spacing.ts`.

### Layout — measured vs code

| Value | Figma | Code | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| Column gap | 179px | `--zimm-scale-4500` = **180px** | rounding, fine |
| Desktop right pad | 142px | `--zimm-scale-3500` = **140px** | 2px off |
| Mobile side pad | 30px (x=30) | `--zimm-scale-800` = **32px** | wrong token — `grid.containerPadding.base` is exactly `30px` |
| **Info column width** | **218px** | **`PDP_OPTIONS_COLUMN_WIDTH = '360px'`** | **142px off** |

Desktop composition: 900 gallery + 179 gap + 218 info + 142 pad = 1439 ≈ 1440.
The code's `1fr 360px` yields a **760px gallery and a 360px info column** — gallery loses
140px, text column gains 142px. The author annotated the constant *"Provisional — no
matching zimm token; pending designer sign-off"*, so this was a known guess; we now have
the measured answer.

Mobile info column 342px at x=30 — matches `grid.containerPadding.base` exactly.
**All layout gaps are identical across breakpoints** (28/44/22/16/8/15/2); only width and
three icon sizes change.

### Design-side defects (all varying residuals — matching values matched at exactly 0px)
- `body2Strong` letter-spacing is **−0.12px** in the repo, **−0.14px** in Figma. The
  correct token **already exists**: `letterSpacings['2xs'] = '-0.00875rem' // -0.14px`
  (`typography.ts:27`). It is a mis-pointed token, not a missing one. **`typography.ts` is
  Tier 1** — UI Designer required.
- `#000000` hardcoded on two labels where everything else uses `text/default`.
- Product name uses a different style on mobile than desktop.
- **Mobile wishlist target is 20×20 — below the WCAG 2.2 AA 24×24 minimum.** (SFCC-434's

The DS Typography collection is mode-switched (`body-2` = 14px desktop / 12px mobile), **but

- **(b) `shared/ui` barrel — confirmed with numbers.** 103 relative re-exports; **212** base

- **(c) Conditional module swap — no PDP equivalent.** The `_app` checkout swap

`overrides/app/utils/sfccImage.ts`'s `proxyImageUrl()` rewrites SFCC image URLs through the
PWA Kit proxy, because direct Demandware-host access is **Cloudflare-WAF-blocked outside the

`origin/feature/SFCC-91_pdp-ui-colour-swatches-variation-selection` branches off SFCC-89 at

### 2e. Concrete path example — a new PDP component per the rules as written

For a hypothetical `PdpSizeSelector`:

```
overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/pdpSizeSelector/
  index.tsx            ← named export PdpSizeSelector + default; props type at top of file
  index.stories.tsx    ← title: 'Commerce/PdpSizeSelector'  (commerce-aware → Commerce/, per components.md)
  index.test.ts        ← only if logic-heavy
overrides/app/theme/components/pdpSizeSelector.ts   ← exports `ZimmPdpSizeSelector` (parts + baseStyle)
overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts             ← add import + key to the `components` object
```

Existing precedent to copy verbatim — `pdpProductInfo` **[V]**:
- Component consumes the recipe via `useMultiStyleConfig('ZimmPdpProductInfo', {})` and applies parts
  as `__css={styles.<part>}` (`pdpProductInfo/index.tsx:27, 32`).
- Recipe declares `parts: ['name','price','description','modelInfo','styleCode']` and a `baseStyle`
  per part (`theme/components/pdpProductInfo.ts:56-90`).
- Values that genuinely can't live in `baseStyle` (conditional margins) are exported as named consts
  from the theme file and imported by the component — `SPACE_DESCRIPTION_TO_META`,
  `SPACE_MODEL_INFO_TO_STYLE_CODE` (`pdpProductInfo.ts:47,50` → `index.tsx:4,42,53`). That is the
  house pattern for "styling that must be at the call site": **name it in the theme file anyway.**
- The theme file carries a header comment explaining each level-4 (`var(--zimm-*)`) escape and why
  no `textStyle` exists for it yet (`pdpProductInfo.ts:1-33`).

**Chakra scale caveat (matters for any new recipe):** `theme/index.ts:51-58` registers only
`borderWidths, breakpoints, colors, fonts, space, textStyles, components`. `fontSizes`, `sizes`, and
`transition` are **deliberately not registered** because Zimmermann and Chakra use the same key names
for different values (`theme/index.ts:26-49`). So `fontSize="2xs"` in a recipe silently resolves to
Chakra's 10px, not Zimmermann's 14px — which is exactly why `pdpProductInfo.ts` uses
`fontSize: 'var(--zimm-font-size-2xs)'`. `spacing` **is** registered as `space`, so `marginBottom: 'l'`
is safe. **[V]**

## 3. The component registry

**What it is:** `scripts/generateRegistry.mjs` (37 kB) scans `overrides/app/{components,hooks,utils,pages}`
**plus** `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/`, and writes markdown tables to
`.claude/registry/{components,hooks,pages,routes,utils}.md` so Claude reads a table instead of grepping.
Columns: Component · Origin · Path · Props · Tier · Squad · Consumers · Last touched · Description. **[V]**

**Does a new PDP component register itself? No — it is fully automatic.** Nothing is hand-maintained
**[V]**:
- `generateRegistry.mjs:670` — `origin: baseMatch ? 'Override' : 'Custom'`, matched by folder-name
  variants (`folderVariants()` at `:105-109` tries kebab↔camel), so a camelCase Zimmermann folder with
  no base twin is auto-classified `Custom`.
- Tier and squad are derived from `.claude/rules/` path lists (`generateRegistry.mjs:~112` onward).
- `scripts/hooks/pre-commit:49-62` regenerates and `git add`s `.claude/registry/` whenever a staged path
  matches `overrides/app/{components,hooks,utils,pages}/` or `routes.tsx`.
- `.claude/settings.json` PostToolUse `Edit|Write` → `.claude/hooks/registryUpdate.sh` → incremental
  `--file=` regen (skips `*.test.*`, `*.stories.*`, `ContentfulDefinition`).
- `package.json` `postinstall` runs `npm run generate:registry`.

**Is it a blocker? No.** The registry is **already on `develop`** (`git ls-tree develop` lists all five
`.claude/registry/*.md`, `scripts/generateRegistry.mjs`, and `.claude/hooks/registryUpdate.sh`) and
therefore on this branch. **[V]** `feature/f2r-component-registry` adds one extra output
(`.claude/registry/mocks.md`) and generator refinements, but nothing the PDP work depends on.

The premise in the task brief that the registry might be "not yet merged to develop" is **false** — it
is merged. **[V]**

Minor: `.claude/registry/components.md:84` shows `ZimmPageToolbar`'s props flattened across its
discriminated union (`variant: 'breadcrumbs', heading: string, …`). Commit `cf17c3d` on this branch
("teach extractTsProps to parse discriminated union Props types") fixes the generator; the checked-in
`.md` is stamped `2026-08-20` and predates it. Cosmetic — a regen will correct it. **[V]**

## 4. Intercept traps — which apply

### (a) base-path import → unstyled base component in Storybook & Vitest

**Mechanism confirmed [V]:**
- `package.json` `ccExtensibility: {extends: '@salesforce/retail-react-app', overridesDir: 'overrides'}`
  — read by the pwa-kit webpack plugin, i.e. **real builds only**.
- `.storybook/main.js:25` aliases `'@salesforce/retail-react-app'` → `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app`,
  bypassing the resolver entirely.
- `vitest.config.ts:17-20` aliases only `~` and `app` — it never mentions
  `@salesforce/retail-react-app`, so those imports go straight to `node_modules` by normal resolution.

**Does it apply to the PDP work today? Not yet.** I cross-referenced every base-path import in
`overrides/` against every existing override directory. The **only** collision in the entire repo is
`icons`, and it is deliberate (`overrides/app/components/icons/index.tsx:73` re-exports from the base
icon set — that's the documented single-source-of-truth pattern; `header/index.tsx:44` imports the
same base path). **[V]**

Every other base-path import in `overrides/` resolves to a module we do **not** override
(`shared/ui`, `constants`, `contexts`, `utils/*`, `seo`, `link`, `loading-spinner`, `search`,
`with-registration`, `product-scroller`, `section`, `hooks/use-multi-site`, `hooks/use-current-basket`,
`hooks/use-navigation`, `hooks/use-einstein`, `app/theme`, `app/routes`, `app/mocks/standard-product`).
Per `overrideStyling.md` that is simply correct. **[V]**

**It becomes live the moment PDP work adds an override.** Concretely: if you create
`overrides/app/components/swatch-group/`, then `product-view/index.jsx:55` imports it by base path —
correct in the app, base-unstyled in Storybook/Vitest. Same for `image-gallery` (`product-view:44,48`),
`display-price` (`product-view:53` + 5 others), `quantity-picker` (`product-view:50`),
`breadcrumb` (**already overridden**, and `product-view/index.jsx:45` imports it by base path — so the
moment anything writes a story or test that renders base `ProductView`, it will render the *base*
breadcrumb, not ours). **[V]**

Rule for new PDP code, per `overrideStyling.md` > "Importing an already-overridden component":
import an already-overridden sibling by **relative path** (`'../breadcrumb'`), never by base path. The
PDP page already does this correctly at `index.tsx:6,8,9` (all relative `../../components/…`). **[V]**

### (b) `shared/ui` barrel — a relative re-export the resolver never rewrites

**Confirmed with hard numbers [V]:**
- `node_modules/…/app/components/shared/ui/index.jsx` is a pure barrel of **103** relative re-exports
  (`export {Box} from './Box'`, `export {Button} from './Button'`, …).
- Base files importing the barrel path `…/components/shared/ui'`: **212**.
- Base files importing a deep `…/components/shared/ui/<Name>` path: **0**.

Because the re-export is relative (`'./Button'`), the `ccExtensibility` resolver — which only rewrites
`@salesforce/retail-react-app/...` specifiers — never sees it. Creating
`overrides/app/components/shared/ui/Button/index.tsx` would intercept **zero** of those 212 consumers.
You would additionally have to override the barrel itself.

**Does the PDP work depend on this? No, and it should not start.** The sub-modules are one-line Chakra
re-exports (`shared/ui/Skeleton/index.jsx` is literally `export {Skeleton} from '@chakra-ui/react'`) —
there is nothing to override there. No `overrides/app/components/shared/` exists on HEAD or `develop`
(`git ls-tree` = 0 on both). The correct lever for `Box`/`Text`/`Skeleton` styling is the Chakra theme,
which is already how the repo does it. **[V]**

Style consistency note: `breadcrumb/index.tsx:3` imports `Box, Text` from `@chakra-ui/react` directly
while `product-detail/index.tsx:5` and `zimmPageToolbar/index.tsx:3` import them from the SFCC
`shared/ui` barrel. Functionally identical (the barrel is a Chakra re-export), but pick one for new
files. **[V]**

### (c) conditional render of an alternate module

**The `_app` checkout swap is real but does not touch PDP [V]:**
`node_modules/…/app/components/_app/index.jsx:216` computes `const isCheckout = /\/checkout$/.test(location?.pathname)`,
then `:403` swaps `Header` → `CheckoutHeader` and `:484` `{!isCheckout ? <Footer /> : <CheckoutFooter />}`.
`/product/:productId` never matches that regex, so PDP always gets the normal Header/Footer.
**No PDP equivalent of this trap exists.** **[V]**

**Two adjacent things worth knowing anyway [V]:**
1. **`<Island hydrateOn='visible'>`.** Base wraps `ProductView`, `InformationAccordion`, and all three
   `RecommendedProducts` in `<Island>` (`product-detail/index.jsx:674, 788, 816, 831, 846`) — deferred
   hydration. Our override uses no Island. If PDP work reintroduces base components, they will hydrate
   eagerly unless Island is reintroduced too. Relevant to the ≤2s p75 mobile LCP budget in AGENTS.md.
2. **Set/bundle branch.** `product-detail/index.jsx:672` renders a structurally different tree for
   `isProductASet || isProductABundle` (per-child `ProductView` + `InformationAccordion`). Our override
   renders one shape for every product type, so a set or bundle SKU will render as a plain product. Not
   an override-bypass — a functional gap. **[V]**
3. `ProductView` is rendered from 6 places, not just PDP (`product-view-modal/index.jsx`,
   `product-view-modal/bundle.jsx`, `bonus-product-view-modal/index.jsx`, + tests). An override of it
   is a Tier-2-scale blast radius, not a PDP-local change. **[V]**

## 5. Data layer

**Rule** (`.claude/rules/components.md` > Composition): anything under `overrides/app/components/`
receives data as props and calls **no** data-fetching hook — not `useProduct`, not any
`@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react` / React Query hook. Fetching lives in `overrides/app/pages/`. **[V]**

**The PDP obeys this today** — `useProduct`/`useCategory` are called only in
`overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx:21-31`; `PdpProductInfo`, `Breadcrumb` and
`ZimmPageToolbar` are all pure prop-driven. **[V]**

**Type chain [V]:**

```
useProduct  →  node_modules/@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react/hooks/ShopperProducts/query.d.ts:28
               UseQueryResult<DataType<Client['getProduct']>>
            →  commerce-sdk-isomorphic ShopperProductsModelTypes.Product
               (node_modules/commerce-sdk-isomorphic/lib/index.esm.d.ts:59783-59835)
```

Fields the PDP already reads, all optional on the type: `id: string` (the only required one), `name?`,
`price?`, `currency?`, `shortDescription?`, `longDescription?`, `primaryCategoryId?`. Also available and
unused: `imageGroups?: Array<ImageGroup>`, `variants?`, `variationAttributes?`, `variationValues?`,
`master?`, `inventory?`/`inventories?`, `type?: ProductType`, `setProducts?`, `bundledProducts?`,
`productPromotions?`, `priceRanges?`, `prices?`, `pageMetaTags?`, `slugUrl?`. **[V]**

**Custom SFCC attributes.** The type ends in `& { [key: string]: any }` (`index.esm.d.ts:59834`), so any
`c_*` attribute typechecks as `any` for free. The repo deliberately does **not** rely on that — it
declares a narrowed intersection type instead:

```ts
// overrides/app/types/commerce.ts:7-10
export type ProductWithSizeFit = NonNullable<ReturnType<typeof useProduct>['data']> & {
  c_sizeFit?: string;
};
```

Used at `product-detail/index.tsx:78` as `(product as ProductWithSizeFit | undefined)?.c_sizeFit`.
**Copy this pattern for every new `c_*` attribute** — add the field to `commerce.ts`, re-export from
`types/index.ts`. It satisfies AGENTS.md > Type Definitions ("don't re-declare types already exported by
`commerce-sdk-isomorphic`") by deriving from `ReturnType<typeof useProduct>` rather than restating it. **[V]**

399	
400	> The PR body describes a different, older state: *"Tests 1, 3, 5, and 9 … are skipped … Tests 6, 7, and 8 require click-through navigation infrastructure or BrowserStack setup."* That no longer matches the code.
401
